hints: Focus on how much carbon is packed into each fuel, since every carbon atom becomes one molecule of CO2 on complete combustion.
Calculate moles of fuel in 10 kg using moles = 10000 / Mr, then multiply by the number of carbons per formula to get moles of CO2.
Compare mass of CO2 = moles of CO2 x 44 for each fuel, and look for the fuel with the highest carbon to mass ratio, remembering oxygen in the formula adds mass without making CO2.
walkthrough:
**Link CO2 to carbon in the fuel**

Think simply: complete combustion turns every C atom into one $\text{CO}_2$ molecule. So more moles of C in 10 kg means more mass of $\text{CO}_2$.

$$\text{moles of CO}_2 = \text{moles of fuel} \times \text{number of C atoms per molecule}$$

**Write the rule for mass of CO2**

For 10 kg = 10000 g of fuel, first find moles of fuel, then scale up to $\text{CO}_2$.

$$\text{mass of CO}_2 = \frac{10000}{M_r \text{ of fuel}} \times n \times 44$$ where $n$ is number of C atoms and 44 is $M_r$ of $\text{CO}_2$.

**Calculate Mr for each fuel**

Let's work out the molar masses quickly.

$$M_r(\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{34}\text{O}_2) = 270, \quad M_r(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}) = 46$$
$$M_r(\text{C}_8\text{H}_{18}) = 114, \quad M_r(\text{C}_3\text{H}_8) = 44$$

**Compare CO2 produced**

The key value is $n / M_r$, the moles of carbon per gram of fuel. Octane has 8 carbons for only 114 mass, giving the largest ratio.

$$\text{octane: } \frac{10000}{114} \times 8 \times 44 \approx 30.9 \text{ kg of CO}_2$$ This beats propane at about 30.0 kg, biodiesel at about 27.7 kg and ethanol at about 19.1 kg.

options.A: Biodiesel has the most carbons per molecule (17), but it also has a very large Mr of 270, including two O atoms that add mass but make no CO2. Its CO2 mass is about 27.7 kg, less than octane. Trap is choosing the biggest formula.
options.B: Ethanol, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}$, contains oxygen and has only 2 carbons per 46 mass units. It gives about 19.1 kg of CO2, the smallest of the four. Oxygenated fuels give less CO2 per kg.
options.C: Octane, $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{18}$, has Mr = 114 and produces 8 moles of CO2 per mole. From 10 kg this gives about 30.9 kg of CO2, the largest because it has a high proportion of carbon and no oxygen to add dead mass.
options.D: Propane, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$, is very close with Mr = 44 and 3 CO2 per mole, giving exactly 30.0 kg of CO2. Students often pick it because the Mr equals CO2, but its carbon ratio is just slightly lower than octane.
